Rashi on Yevamot 11b:12:1.hebrew: היתה אחת כשרה - מי שנפלו לפניו שתי יבמות מאח אחד, ביאתה או חליצתה של אחת מהן פוטרת צרתה. היתה אחת כשרה ואחת פסולה וכו':
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:12:1.english: One was fit - [In the case of] one before whom two yevamot fell [for levirate marriage] from one brother, the intercourse or chalitzah of one of them exempts her rival wife. [If] one was fit and one was disqualified, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:13:1.english: Fit for all - [She is] of [unblemished] lineage and fit for the priesthood.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:13:2.english: Disqualified for all - For example, where she was a divorcee or a chalutzah from another husband, and [thus] disqualified from the priesthood.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:13:3.english: Since for him she is suitable - For he is an Israelite.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:13:4.hebrew: מאי נפקא ליה מינה - הי דליבעי לחלוץ, ואי בעי לייבם, הי דליבעי לייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:13:4.english: What difference does it make to him - Whichever one he wishes, let him perform chalitzah [with her], and if he wishes to perform yibum, whichever one he wishes, let him perform yibum [with her].

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:14:1.hebrew: פסולה פסולה ליה - וכשרה לעלמא, לכל העולם. ומאי ניהו? כגון שהחזיר אחיו גרושתו ולו אשה אחרת, ומת, דהוי הגרושה פסולה לזה, שאינה ראויה לאחיו. ואשמועינן דאע"ג דכתיב בה טומאה, צרתה כשרה, דכתיב "היא תועבה". דאי שאר חייבי לאוין, כגון אלמנה לכ"ג וגרושה לכהן הדיוט, מאי אתא לאשמעינן:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:14:1.english: Disqualified [means] disqualified for him - And fit for the general public, [that is,] for everyone [else]. And what is [that case]? For example, where his brother remarried his divorcée, and he had another wife, and he died, so that the divorcée is disqualified for this [surviving brother], since she is not fit for his [deceased] brother. And [the Mishnah] teaches us that even though "defilement" is written concerning her, her rival wife is fit, as it is written, "she is an abomination." For if [it were referring to] other [women prohibited by] negative commandments — such as a widow to a High Priest or a divorcée to an ordinary priest — what would [it] be coming to teach us?

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:15:1.english: Disqualified in general - [Disqualified] from the priesthood.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:16:1.hebrew: כאן שנה רבי - במשנה זו דקתני חולץ לפסולה, למדנו רבי: לא ישפוך אדם מי בורו אע"פ שאין צריך להם, ואחרים צריכים להם; כגון הכא, מכיון דיכול לחלוץ לפסולה ותפטר הכשרה, לא יחלוץ לכשרה ויפסלנה לכהונה. והא דרב יוסף בפ' החולץ (לקמן יבמות מד.) עלה דהא משנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:16:1.english: Here Rabbi taught - In this Mishnah, which teaches [that] he performs ḥalitzah for the disqualified one, Rabbi taught us [that] a person should not pour out the water of his cistern, even though he has no need for it, while others need it; such as here: since he can perform ḥalitzah for the disqualified one and [thereby] the fit one is exempted, he should not perform ḥalitzah for the fit one and disqualify her from [marrying into] the priesthood. And this [statement] of Rav Yosef is in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 44a), [stated] regarding this Mishnah.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:17:1.hebrew: היא וצרתה ס"ד - חליצה לתרוייהו למה לי:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:17:1.english: She and her rival wife, can it enter your mind - Why do I need ḥalitza for both of them?

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:19:1.english: What is [the law regarding] her rival wife - With respect to levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:1:1.hebrew: ולא מתייבמת - טעמא מפרש בפ"ק דסוטה. [קתני מיהא] חולצת, קשיא לרב:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:1:1.english: And [she] may not enter into levirate marriage - The reason is explained in the first chapter of Sotah. [In any case, it teaches] "she performs chalitzah" — [this is] a difficulty for Rav.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:20:1.hebrew: במותר לה - בעלה זה שמת, נאסרה תחלה כשנשאת לשני, וחזר הראשון והחזירה באיסור, ולמחר מת:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:20:1.english: To the one permitted to her - [Namely,] this husband of hers who died: she first became forbidden [to him] when she married a second [man], and the first [husband] went back and remarried her in [violation of the] prohibition, and the next day he died.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:20:2.hebrew: באסור לה - כגון יבמה, לא כ"ש:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:20:2.english: To one who is forbidden to her - Such as her yavam, [is it] not all the more so?

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:20:3.hebrew: מי אלים ק"ו - האי ק"ו דאמרן, במותר לה נאסרה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:20:3.english: Is [the] a fortiori inference strong [enough] - [This refers to] this a fortiori inference that we stated: "To one who was permitted to her, she became forbidden."

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:2:1.english: Following marriage - After she was married to another [man] and he died or divorced her.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:2:2.english: She is forbidden - to return to the first [husband].

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:2:3.hebrew: מן האירוסין - שנתארסה לאחר ומת, מותרת לחזור לראשון:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:2:3.english: Following betrothal - [Meaning] that she became betrothed to another [man] and he died, she is permitted to return to the first [husband].

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:2:4.english: She was defiled - She had sexual relations.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:3:1.hebrew: אחת זו ואחת זו אסורה - דכתיב ״והיתה לאיש אחר״, והויה היינו קידושין, וכתיב ״לא יוכל בעלה הראשון אשר שלחה״ וגו':
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:3:1.english: Both this one and that one are forbidden - For it is written: "And she becomes another man's [wife]" — and "becoming" means betrothal — and it is written: "Her former husband, who sent her away, may not [take her again]," etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:5:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei - Who establishes the entire verse [as referring] to one who remarries his divorced wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:5:2.hebrew: לאו בסוטה - המזנה תחת בעלה לית ליה, ואפילו פשיטא לן דזנאי:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:5:2.english: A prohibition in [the case of] a sotah - [one] who commits adultery under her husband, he does not hold [that there is a prohibition], and even [when] it is certain to us that she committed adultery.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:6:1.hebrew: מ"ט הויה ואישות כתיב בה - באותה הנאסרה לבעלה, יש בה הויה, דכתיב: "והיתה לאיש אחר", אישות, דכתיב: "או כי ימות האיש האחרון". "לא יוכל בעלה הראשון" — משניסת לאחר על ידי קידושין ואישות, וכגון דגירשה הראשון, הוא דקאי קמא ב"לא יוכל", אבל מזנה תחתיו — לא:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:6:1.english: What is the reason? Becoming and matrimony are written regarding her - Regarding that [woman] who becomes forbidden to her husband, there is "becoming" [i.e., betrothal] in her [case], as it is written: "and she becomes another man's" [Deut. 24:2], [and] "matrimony," as it is written: "or if the latter husband dies [who took her to be his wife]" [Deut. 24:3]. "Her first husband may not [take her again]" [Deut. 24:4] — [that is,] once she has married another [man] through betrothal and matrimony, and in a case where the first [husband] divorced her, [it is then] that the first [husband] stands under [the prohibition of] "may not," whereas [regarding] one who commits adultery under him, [she is] not.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:7:1.hebrew: צרתה מהו - להתייבם. צרתה כמותה, וגמיר טומאה מעריות:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:7:1.english: What is [the law of] her rival wife - [Whether she may] enter into levirate marriage. "Her rival wife is like her" — [this is because] he derives "defilement" from forbidden relations.

Rashi on Yevamot 11b:8:1.hebrew: ואי משום דכתיב בה תועבה היא - דמשמע מיעוטא — היא ולא צרתה — איכא למידרש מיעוטא אבניה, דאין בתה הימנו פסולה לכהונה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11b:8:1.english: And if [it is] because it is written concerning her, “she is an abomination” - which implies an exclusion — she, and not her rival wife — one can expound the exclusion [as referring] to her children, [meaning] that her daughter from him is not disqualified from [marrying into] the priesthood.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:12:1.hebrew: אמר ליה תניתוה - למיפשט בעיא קמייתא הוא דאתא, דלאיכא דאמרי דפשיטא ליה לרבנן כיון דאיתעקר איתעקר, איכא למימר דאתיא כרבנן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:12:1.english: He said to him: You learned it - It comes to resolve the first [version of the] dilemma, for according to the ika de'amrei [version], where it is obvious regarding the Rabbis that "once it is uprooted, it is uprooted," one can say that [this baraita] follows the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:17:1.hebrew: או היא או צרתה - אע"ג דחליצה פסולה צריך לחזור [על כל האחין], היינו דוקא כגון חלץ לאחיות דלא נפטרו צרות, וכן חלץ לבעלת הגט לא נפטרה צרה, דהורע הזיקה וקלשה לה; אבל בשאר דוכתי, דאע"ג דאסורה להתייבם, כיון שהזיקה שלימה — פוטרת:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:17:1.english: Either she or her rival wife - Even though [in the case of] an invalid ḥalitza one must go around [to all the brothers], that is specifically [in cases] such as where he performed ḥalitza with sisters, where the rival wives are not exempted, and similarly [where] he performed ḥalitza with a woman who received a bill of divorce, [where] the rival wife is not exempted, because the levirate bond was impaired and weakened; but in other places, where even though she is forbidden to enter into levirate marriage, since the levirate bond is intact, [her ḥalitza] exempts [her rival wife].

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:18:1.hebrew: לאו תרוצי קא מתרצת לה תריץ הכי - תימה: במאי מתרץ לה? דאע"ג דבעי למימר "או היא או צרתה", שייך למיתני שפיר "היא וצרתה", כמו "חלץ ועשה בה מאמר". ובפ' נערה בנדרים (דף סו:), דקתני "אביה ובעלה מפירין נדריה", איצטריך למתני סיפא: "הפר האב ולא הפר הבעל, הפר הבעל ולא הפר האב — אין מופר", דלא תימא "אביה ובעלה" — "אביה או בעלה" קאמר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:18:1.english: [And] are you not emending it? Emend [it] thus - [This is] astonishing: in what [way] is he emending it? For even though [the baraita] means to say "either she or her rival wife," it is perfectly appropriate to teach "she and her rival wife," just like "[if] he performed ḥalitza and ma'amar [betrothal] with her." And in chapter Na'arah in Nedarim (66b), where it teaches, "Her father and her husband annul her vows," it was necessary to teach the latter clause: "If the father annulled and the husband did not annul, [or] the husband annulled and the father did not annul, it is not annulled," so that you should not say that "her father and her husband" means "her father or her husband."

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:20:1.hebrew: מי אלים ק"ו למידחי לצרה - לאוסרה לייבום קא מיבעיא ליה, דלפוטרה מן החליצה לא מהני קל וחומר אפילו להיא גופה, כדאמרינן פ"ק דסוטה (דף ו. ושם), דספק סוטה חולצת ולא מתייבמת משום ק"ו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:20:1.english: Is [the] kal vachomer strong enough to push aside the rival wife - He raises the dilemma [only] with regard to forbidding her from levirate marriage, for to exempt her from chalitzah, a kal vachomer is not effective even for [the woman] herself, as we say in the first chapter of Sotah (6a and there), that a safek sotah [a woman suspected of adultery] performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage because of a kal vachomer.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:21:1.hebrew: מי אמרינן ק"ו במקום מצוה כו' - וא"ת, תפשוט מפ"ק דסוטה (דף ב.), דקתני "חולצת ולא מתייבמת", ומפרש בגמ' משום ק"ו? וי"ל: דאיכא התם טעמא אחרינא, כדמפרש התם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:21:1.english: "Do we say [an] a fortiori [inference applies] in place of a mitzvah, etc." - And if you ask: resolve [the dilemma] from the first chapter of Sotah (2a), where it teaches: "she performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage," and it explains in the Gemara [that this is] because of an a fortiori [inference]? And one can answer: there is another reason there, as it explains there.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:3:1.hebrew: לרבות סוטה שנסתרה - וא"ת: והיכי מפקי רבנן קרא מפשטיה, דפשטיה דקרא במחזיר גרושתו כתיב? וי"ל, דלא מסתבר להו למיקרי טומאה לנישואי גרושה, כיון דבעילתה היתר היא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:3:1.english: To include a sotah who secluded herself - And if you should ask: How do the Rabbis remove the verse from its plain meaning, for the plain meaning of the verse is written regarding one who takes back his divorcee? And one can answer that it does not seem reasonable to them to call the marriage of a divorcee "defilement," since her intercourse [with her second husband] is permitted.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:4:1.hebrew: מאי נסתרה נבעלה - וא"ת, וכיון דלא כתיב לאו בסוטה ספק, אמאי אמר בסוטה (דף ז.) דאם בא עליה בעלה בדרך, לוקה? וי"ל: דלחומרא עשה הכתוב ספק כודאי, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:4:1.english: What [does] "secluded herself" [mean]? She engaged in relations - And if you will say: Since no negative prohibition is written regarding an uncertain sotah, why does [the Gemara] state in Sotah (7a) that if her husband has relations with her on the way [to Jerusalem], he receives lashes? One can say [in answer] that as a stringency, Scripture treated an uncertain case like a definite case, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:6:1.hebrew: הויה ואישו' כתיב בה - פי' בקונטרס דההוא ענינא במחזיר גרושתו כתיב. ותימה, דפשיטא דבמחזיר גרושתו איירי קרא, ואפילו רבנן לא פליגי. ונראה לרשב"א לפרש ד"הויה ואישות כתיב בה" — פירוש או "הוטמאה", דכתיב: "לא יוכל בעלה הראשון אשר שלחה לשוב לקחתה להיות לו לאשה אחרי אשר הוטמאה"; אלמא במחזיר גרושתו איירי, ד"אחרי אשר הוטמאה" אלהיות לו לאשה קאי, דבסוטה לא שייך הויה ואישות, שהרי לא גירשה מעולם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:6:1.english: Becoming and matrimony are written in it - Rashi explained that that passage is written regarding one who remarries his divorcée. And [this is] astonishing, for it is obvious that the verse speaks of one who remarries his divorcée, and even the Rabbis do not disagree [about that]. And it appears to the Rashba to explain that "becoming and matrimony are written in it" means [that it refers to] "she was defiled," as it is written: "Her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife after she was defiled" — thus it speaks of one who remarries his divorcée, for "after she was defiled" refers to "to be his wife," for in [the case of] a sotah, becoming and matrimony do not apply, since he never divorced her.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:7:1.hebrew: צרתה מהו - היא גופה לא מיבעי ליה, דלר' יוסי בן כיפר ודאי פטורה מן החליצה ומן הייבום, דטומאה כתיב בה כעריות; ולרבנן נמי היא גופה פשיטא דחולצת ולא מתייבמת, דאפי' אם תמצא לומר כיון דאיתעקר איתעקר, אינה מתייבמת מק"ו: דהשתא במותר לה נאסרה, באסור לה לא כ"ש? ואת"ל נמי דאין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו, אין לפוטרה מן החליצה, כיון דעיקר קרא דטומאה בסוטה כתיב ולא במחזיר גרושתו, משום דלא מסתברא למיקרי טומאה נישואי גרושה, כדפרישית לעיל. וכן משמע לקמן דקאמר: "אלא או היא או צרתה חולצת", ובעי למיפשט דלרבנן אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו, ואפילו הכי אין פוטרתה מחליצה, כדפרישית. אבל צרתה בעי: לר' יוסי בן כיפר, אם פטורה מן החליצה או אפילו מתייבמת; ולרבנן בעי אי מתייבמת — דפשיטא ליה דלא אלים קל וחומר למידחי צרה — או חולצת ולא מתייבמת, משום דאין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11b:7:1.english: What is [the law regarding] her rival wife? - [Regarding] her herself, he [Rav Yehuda] does not raise a dilemma: for according to Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar, she is certainly exempt from chalitzah and from yibbum, since "defilement" is written regarding her as [it is regarding] forbidden relations [arayot]; and according to the Rabbis as well, [regarding] her herself, it is obvious that she performs chalitzah and does not enter into yibbum. For even if you say that "once [the verse] is uprooted, it is [completely] uprooted," she does not enter into yibbum by an a fortiori argument: if now, [when she was married] to one permitted to her, she became forbidden [to her first husband], [when she is married] to one forbidden to her, is it not all the more so [that she is forbidden to the yavam]? And even if you say that "a verse does not depart from its plain meaning," one should not exempt her from chalitzah, since the primary verse of "defilement" is written regarding a sotah and not regarding one who remarries his divorcée, because it is not logical to call the marriage of a divorcée "defilement," as I explained above. And so it is implied below, where [the Gemara] says: "Rather, either she or her rival wife performs chalitzah," and seeks to resolve [from there] that according to the Rabbis a verse does not depart from its plain meaning, and even so it does not exempt her from chalitzah, as I have explained. Rather, [it is regarding] her rival wife that he raises the dilemma: according to Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar, whether she is exempt from chalitzah or even enters into yibbum; and according to the Rabbis, he asks whether she enters into yibbum — for it is obvious to him that an a fortiori argument is not strong enough to push aside a rival wife — or whether she performs chalitzah and does not enter into yibbum, because a verse does not depart from its plain meaning.
